newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil down in volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil down in volatile trade.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps edged down late afternoon on Thursday in a day of volatile trade as the market rose and ebbed on mixed news of low stocks and a weak IPE open, traders said.
"The market is volatile, it was bearish on the IPE but bullish on the low stocks," one broker said.

April gas oil was last quoted down about 10 cents from Wednesday at $26.60/$26.80 per barrel, brokers said. The market opened to trade this morning at $26.70, peaking at $26.90 this afternoon before edging down, they said.
May gas oil trading was much more hectic with deals done in the morning at $25.30, $25.40, $25.45 and $25.52 before slipping to trade at $25.25 in the afternoon, brokers said.
May was last quoted at $25.25/$25.45 per barrel, down about 30 cents from Wednesday.
Overnight May Brent crude lost a hefty 60 cents to close at $18.51 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange and lost further ground on Thursday to last trade down 17 cents to $18.34.
Gas oil on the IPE also fell to last trade at $163.00 per tonne, down 2.50 from Wednesday.
Traders said the market is taking a breather waiting for the physical acitivity to start late in the day.
The April jet fuel/gas oil regrade was quoted at -85/-70 cents and traded earlier in the day at -83 cents, brokers said.
Fuel oil swaps edged down slightly in thin trading with April last quoted at $99.00/$100.00, down about $1.50 from Thursday.
